method: Built-in image_gen; reference atlases retained unchanged; separate tail strips.
arrow: Create a new transparent game VFX sprite strip, using the attached arrow atlas ONLY as palette and hand-painted style reference. Output exactly THREE equal square cells in ONE horizontal row, a 3:1 wide image. No visible grid, labels, border, arrow body, projectile, or background. Each cell shows an age of ONE VERY SHORT cyan/turquoise energy ribbon segment. All three segments are perfectly horizontal along +X, same centre and EXACTLY THE SAME LEFT AND RIGHT EXTENTS (roughly x=20%..80% of each cell); they differ only in vertical thickness and internal wispy texture. First cell: fresh short stroke, soft turquoise shoulders around a slender pale cyan core, height about 12% of cell, mildly irregular ink-painted edges. Middle cell: same length, thinner stroke, height about 8%, airy textured edges. Third cell: same length, delicate thin stroke, height about 4%. Keep all three visible and fairly opaque; runtime will perform the fade. Ends have very short rounded soft tapers, not long pointed spears. Make the central 80% of each stroke uniformly usable for overlap with neighbouring short strokes. Flat 2D side view, no curve, no diagonal, no arc, no flare, no detached dots, no shadows. These are connected wake tiles, NOT miniature complete comet trails. Preserve fully transparent alpha everywhere outside the strokes.
heavy: Create a new transparent game VFX sprite strip, using the attached cracked purple stone-ball atlas ONLY as style and color reference. Output THREE equal square cells in ONE horizontal row, 3:1 wide image. No grid, labels, text, background, border, projectile head or stone ball. Each cell is the ageing of one broad, compact magical energy wake puff behind the stone orb. It points to the RIGHT (+X): the right attachment end is broad and rounded, the left trailing edge breaks into short irregular wisps. First cell: dense short plump oval tuft approximately 70% cell width and 56% cell height, muted violet/purple-charcoal vapor with a modest lavender inner glow; rough ink-and-gouache texture matching the head's purple fissures. The tuft should feel weighty, filled and turbulent, broad enough to match most of the stone ball's width. Middle cell: same centred puff now slightly smaller, more diffuse and fragmented, still broad, purple fading toward smoky grey-violet. Third cell: soft small broken violet haze remnant, same centre. No crescent moon shape, no sickle, no ring, no long thin flame, no white-hot core, no pink neon, no large floating rock chip. A few extremely fine charcoal dust flecks embedded in the puff are okay, but the main silhouette is one cohesive vapor lobe. Keep generous transparent gutters around each cell. Transparent alpha background, crisp painted texture inside soft transparent outer edges, consistent orthographic side view and anchor.
